changes.after: Require_once loads a file and remembers that it was already loaded.

before: require evaluates the target PHP file; an unavailable required file causes an Error. The include warning/false alternative is a reference only, not an additional hands-on operation here. Use explicit trusted paths, never user input as executable include paths.

require_once skips evaluating a file already included. __DIR__ is the directory of the current source file, so the fixture does not depend on the shell working directory. Loading twice with plain require repeats its side effect. Save helper.php beside main.php with this complete content:
```php
<?php
echo "loaded\n";
```

With the same trusted helper.php shown above beside this companion, plain require evaluates that file each time. Its input is the explicit local path; its observable effect here is two output lines, unlike require_once.
```php
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/helper.php';
require __DIR__ . '/helper.php';
```
Expected output: loaded; loaded.
Expected output or behavior: loaded. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
